title: Follow-ups: API keys, and installing Claude Code only when it is needed

steps.page: API keys on the sign-in screen
steps.intro: You asked whether other API keys work. They do, in Settings, but the sign-in screen only takes an Anthropic one. These decide what it should take.

steps.path: The small "Use an API key" link under the sign-in buttons
steps.headline: Should the sign-in screen's API key box accept any kind of key the app supports?
steps.today: Settings, Assistant settings, Cloud providers, "Your own API keys" accepts Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and OpenRouter keys. The sign-in screen's box accepts only an Anthropic key.
steps.problem: Someone who pays for an OpenAI or Google key cannot use it to get through setup, even though the app would run on it once they reached Settings.
steps.proposal: Choose how the box handles the different kinds of key.

options.label: Recognise it
options.summary: One box: paste any key and the app works out whose it is from how it starts, asking "Which service is this key for?" only when it cannot tell.
pros: Nothing to choose first; paste and continue.
Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and OpenRouter keys each start in a recognisable way.
cons: An unusual key gets one extra question after pasting.

options.label: Pick the service first
options.summary: A row of four choices (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, OpenRouter) above the box.
pros: Always clear which service the key is for.
cons: One more step, and a small link opens into a bigger panel.

options.label: Anthropic only
options.summary: Leave the box as it is; other keys are added in Settings after setup.
pros: No change to this part of the screen.
cons: Anyone with only an OpenAI or Google key still cannot get through setup.

steps.path: Pasting an Anthropic API key into the sign-in screen's box
steps.headline: Should an Anthropic key run on Claude Code, or on YouCoded's own assistant?
steps.today: An Anthropic key pasted at setup is handed to Claude Code. A key added in Settings instead runs on YouCoded's own assistant, which does not need Claude Code installed.
steps.problem: Under your answer that Claude Code installs only when someone chooses Claude, an Anthropic key would force that install just to use the key.
steps.proposal: Choose which assistant a key pasted at setup runs on.

options.label: YouCoded's own assistant
options.summary: Every key, Anthropic included, runs on YouCoded's own assistant; nothing extra installs.
pros: All four kinds of key behave the same way.
Fastest way through setup for anyone with a key.
cons: Someone who wanted Claude Code specifically has to sign in with Claude instead, or add it later.

options.label: Claude Code
options.summary: An Anthropic key installs Claude Code first, then runs on it, as today.
pros: Matches what the key does today.
cons: The one kind of key that makes setup wait for an install.
Anthropic keys behave differently at setup than in Settings.

steps.path: The Log in with OpenRouter button
steps.headline: Should Log in with OpenRouter take an OpenRouter key, now that keys work?
steps.today: Pressing Log in with OpenRouter only shows "OpenRouter sign-in is coming in a later update." An OpenRouter key already works in Settings.
steps.problem: A button that does nothing is the first thing some new users press, while the thing they came for already works elsewhere.
steps.proposal: Choose what the button does until a real OpenRouter sign-in exists.

options.label: Open the key box
options.summary: The button opens the API key box with a line on where to get an OpenRouter key.
pros: Uses the box from the question above, so nothing extra is built.
cons: "Log in" slightly overpromises: it is a key, not a sign-in page.

options.label: Remove the button
options.summary: Only Claude, ChatGPT and local models remain as buttons; OpenRouter keys go through the key link.
pros: Shorter card, and no button that overpromises.
cons: OpenRouter is harder to spot for people looking for it.

options.label: Leave it
options.summary: Keep the "coming in a later update" line until a real sign-in is built.
cons: Still a button that does nothing useful.

steps.page: Installing Claude Code only when someone chooses Claude
steps.intro: You asked that Claude Code install only when someone actually signs in with it. These settle what that means around it.

steps.path: The install checklist a new install runs before the sign-in screen
steps.headline: Should Node and Git still install for everyone, with only Claude Code waiting until someone chooses Claude?
steps.today: Setup installs Node, Git and Claude Code, in that order, before the sign-in screen. YouCoded's own assistant needs none of them to chat.
steps.problem: Node also runs the Terminal view and Claude's sign-in, and Git installs the plugins that come with the app, syncing and the Git panel. Skipping them loses those for everyone who skips.
steps.proposal: Choose which of the three wait until someone chooses Claude.

options.label: Only Claude Code waits
options.summary: Node and Git still install up front; Claude Code installs when someone presses Log in with Claude.
pros: Terminal view, built-in plugins, syncing and the Git panel work for every user.
Signing in with Claude later only needs the one install.
cons: Local and ChatGPT users still wait for Node and Git at setup.

options.label: Node waits too
options.summary: Only Git installs up front; Node and Claude Code install together when someone chooses Claude.
pros: A shorter setup for local and ChatGPT users.
cons: Terminal view does not work for them until Node is installed.

options.label: All three wait
options.summary: Setup installs nothing for local and ChatGPT users.
pros: The fastest possible setup for them.
cons: No Terminal view, no built-in plugins, no syncing and no Git panel until they install them somehow.

steps.risk: Git failing to install today stops setup entirely; it would still do so for everyone under every option here.

steps.path: Choosing a Claude model later, when Claude Code was never installed
steps.headline: When someone without Claude Code chooses Claude later in the app, what should they see?
steps.today: Claude models appear greyed out with "Claude Code not installed", and the Claude card in Settings says "Restart YouCoded to run setup again".
steps.problem: Under this change a restart would not run setup again, so that advice would send people in a circle, and nothing offers to install it.
steps.proposal: Choose where the install is offered.

options.label: An Install button there
options.summary: The Claude card and the greyed model rows get an "Install Claude Code" button that installs it and then starts the Claude sign-in.
pros: Fixed where they notice it, in one press.
Replaces advice that would no longer be true.
cons: A second place that shows install progress, besides setup.

options.label: Back to the sign-in screen
options.summary: The button reopens the setup sign-in screen, which installs it when they press Log in with Claude.
pros: Only one screen ever installs Claude Code.
cons: Leaves the app and returns to a setup screen, which feels like starting over.

steps.headline: Log in with Claude now installs Claude Code first, on the same card, then opens the browser to sign in.
steps.changed: Stated, not asked: the install that used to run before the sign-in screen now runs after pressing Log in with Claude, with its progress shown on the card.
steps.notice: Claude users wait the same total time as today, just after the click instead of before the screen. If the install fails, the card says why and offers Try again.
steps.risk: Not yet confirmed: a freshly installed Claude Code may not be found until the app restarts. If so, the card will say that plainly rather than fail silently.
